about: Codex's acceptance condition for launch (NEXT-VERSION item 59): integer-dollar reconciliation by appropriation, fiscal year, service, requirement, month, CR half and funding lane across every applicable visual and export, with a map of what is proven, what does not apply and what remains. Every surface registered in tools/money-coverage.mjs and every surface the trace matrix harvests is a row; each of the seven dimensions is a cell. A cell is proven only by checks that hold that dimension at the grain the surface prints it, to the dollar: a total does not prove the breakdown beneath it, a cross-foot does not prove the rows it adds, and a figure compared in $M is not compared to the dollar. What remains open is listed for Brad to build or defer explicitly — nothing here is treated as satisfied silently.

dimensions.label: Appropriation
dimensions.carried: the surface prints money for more than one appropriation, or reads another appropriation's board or rows
dimensions.proven: each appropriation's figures are held to that appropriation's own board or data

dimensions.label: Fiscal year
dimensions.carried: the surface prints more than one fiscal year, or reads a year other than the one on screen (a lock, another year's state, imported rows)
dimensions.proven: each year's figures are held to that year's own state, on a board where the years differ

dimensions.label: Service
dimensions.carried: any figure is broken out by service (a row or a column per service)
dimensions.proven: every per-service figure, at every grain it is printed (per requirement, per office, in total), is held

dimensions.label: Requirement
dimensions.carried: any figure is printed for one requirement
dimensions.proven: every requirement's figures are held, and the right requirements are listed

dimensions.label: Month
dimensions.carried: money is placed in fiscal months (October–September, UNSCHEDULED, an obligation Month or Date)
dimensions.proven: every month's figure is held, from the fixture's award dates or the one placement rule

dimensions.label: CR half
dimensions.carried: money is placed in the twelve October–March half-month windows
dimensions.proven: every window's figure is held, from each award's own date

dimensions.label: Funding lane
dimensions.carried: discretionary and mandatory are stated apart (drawn, budget authority, allocated, a lane's own line)

reasons.oneAppn: Built on one appropriation's page from that page's own state — the engine holds one appropriation per page (DATA, SVC and S are its constants) — so it prints no other appropriation's money.
reasons.oneYear: States the year on screen only, from S; it reads no other year's state.
reasons.noTime: Places no money in time: no month, no date, no window.
reasons.monthsNotHalf: Places money in fiscal months; the October–March half-month windows are crData's.
reasons.halfNotMonth: Its time axis is the twelve October–March half-month windows (the CR-half column), not fiscal months.
reasons.lanesCombined: States funded money as discretionary + mandatory together; no figure is one lane on its own.
reasons.totalsOnly: States portfolio totals; no figure is broken out by service.
reasons.noReq: States no figure for a single requirement.
reasons.notMoney: The money-coverage REGISTRY records that this surface carries no money (its reason is quoted above); nothing to reconcile.

findings.title: The workbook writer keeps two decimals, so a sheet printed in $M or $K is not whole dollars in the file
findings.detail: buildXlsx writes every non-integer number as Math.round(v*100)/100. Sheets in dollars are unaffected (their figures are whole). Three are not in dollars: the Two-Plan Forecast ($M → to $10,000), the ATR/BTR log ($M as typed → to $10,000) and the 1A9A CR cash return ($K → to $10). Their figures are right before the writer; the file holds the rounding. The deck is the same kind of thing by design (fSM) and is mapped at its display precision. Fixed in v1.95 (item 60): buildXlsx stores the figure as it is (to 15 significant digits, Excel's own precision) and the cell's number format keeps the display; a fraction in a style with no format gets that style's two-decimal twin. Proven by w7.f1 (the three files, to the dollar) and w7.writer.
findings.observed: 3 Oct 2026, the files read back with the board's own reader (xlsxRead): the Two-Plan Forecast's SE line, 0.085069 on the sheet, is 0.09 in the file; a reprogramming entry typed 1.2345 ($M) is 1.23; the 1A9A cells for $124,458 and $85,069 are 124.46 and 85.07 ($K).

findings.title: The Spend Plan Source dates an incremental award's whole line by its first increment as stored
findings.detail: srcRowsOf takes when = aw.inc[0].d (the first increment in the array, unsorted) and the day from the award object (which an increment does not carry, so the 1st). All of the line's money is dated there, though the increments land in other months. v1.94 fixed the same rule for the 1A9A OBL DATE (crObl sorts with awdCmp and uses awdDay); the Spend Plan Source was not changed. Fixed in v1.95 (item 60), Brad's option (a): an incremental award goes out a line per increment, each dated the day landSvc() places it on and carrying its own part of each lane; what the awards do not cover goes out on 31 August. Proven by w7.f2.
findings.observed: 3 Oct 2026, srcRowsOf on a board whose award for A holds increments stored March (day 3) then November (day 9): both of A's lines (USAF $300, ANG $100) are dated 1 March 2027; the forecast places USAF $200 and ANG $100 in November and USAF $100 in March.

findings.title: An office's share of a requirement split by its CLINs is a fraction of a dollar
findings.detail: pmoSharesOf gives each office CLIN-weighted fractions of PRIME-3, per service, and the by-office views multiply the draw by them: the PMO Matrix, the PMO tabs and the forecast by PMO were seen to carry cents (the file writes them to two decimals); the CR panel by PMO uses the same shares (read in the code, not run). The rule for money everywhere else is whole dollars, spread with apportion(). Fixed in v1.95 (item 60): every by-office figure comes from pmoPartsOf(), in whole dollars by apportion() — the ask, then discretionary, mandatory and unfunded, and the months award by award — so a $100 draw split 1:2 is $67 and $33 on every surface. Proven by w7.f4.
